title: CI strict check disarms a human-confirmed veto: the PR's own commit makes the decision stale
observation: In `hunch check --base <ref> --strict` (the mode the generated CI Hunch Guard runs), a human-confirmed, pattern-tier rejected-alternative veto is rendered advisory and does not count toward the strict fail. The staleness input is lastChangeDate(file) at HEAD; on the PR branch HEAD already contains the PR's own edit to the decision's related file, so the decision looks changed-after-verified (stale) and isVetoBlocker returns false. The same change checked with --staged (pre-commit) still blocks as human-confirmed, and a precise constraint (match regex) keeps blocking because it is staleness-immune. Net: in CI a veto alone would not fail the PR. Mechanism is inferred from code (strictgate.ts isVetoBlocker stale gate + hunchStore.staleness); symptom verified. Scout confirmed no test covers veto + --base --strict.
evidence: demo repo (ip-limit branch, dec_ef1f2ef156 tripwire /req\.ip/ human-confirmed): `hunch check --base main --format markdown` -> '⛔ dec_ef1f2ef156 rejected this approach **(human-confirmed)**'; same + `--public-only` -> human-confirmed; same + `--strict` -> '⚠ ... _(advisory)_'
`hunch check --staged --strict` on the same change -> '⛔ ... (human-confirmed)' and '+ 1 reversed-decision veto(es)', exit 1
